newsitem.title: USA: Elcotel, Technology to merge. [CORRECTED 23:10 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Elcotel, Technology to merge. [CORRECTED 23:10 GMT]

text.p: Elcotel Inc said Wednesday that it will merge with Technology Service Group Inc in order to better compete in the payphone business.

Elcotel, which sells microprocessor-based "intelligent" payphones and network management systems to private payphone operators, said in a statement it will give Technology shareholders 1.05 shares of common stock for every one they hold in their company.
Elcotel's stock was halted from trading on the Nasdaq following the announcement, its last sale at 6-1/4.

Technology, an Atlanta, Georgia provider of microprocessor-based intelligent pay phones and network management systems to regulated public telephone companies, also saw its stock halted, with its last trade at 6-7/8.

"The merger fulfills a strategic initiative...to diversify their businesses and establish a strong presence in the two domestic public communications markets represented by the regulated telephone company payphone operations and the independent private pay phone operations," it said.
"At the same time, the two companies bring together complementary coin, card, wireline, and wireless payphone technologies to address rapidly expanding international markets," it added.
Elcotel said it did not expect the merger to cause much of a disturbance to the operations of either company.
"Many of these functions will continue to be managed and operated by current personnel in their existing facilities," it said, adding that a new name had yet to be chosen.

It said its president and chief operating officer, Tracey Gray, will become president and chief executive officer of the merged companies, while Shelton James, its chairman and chief executive officer, will become chairman.
Vincent Bisceglia, Technology's president and chief executive officer, will become executive vice president and chief operating officer, it added.
Gray later told Reuters he expected the deal, whose value he estimated at $30 million, to close by early November at the latest.

He said very few people from Technology will be transferred to the new company's head offices in Sarasota. He said Technology's facilities will be maintained and only senior officials will move to the new office.
(Corrects to make clear not all employees and facilities are moving).
